Hi Sanjay —

Great to hear from you and appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below — copying Ben and Rishi so we can coordinate artifacts and legal touches.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in 2025 and our Type II audit is currently in progress with an expected report delivery in Q1 2027. I've attached a one-page summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) that outlines scope, controls, and expected report date.

2) Incident response & breach notification: high-level timeline below (this is our standard SLA we can formalize in a playbook):
   - Detection and internal triage: immediate (0–24 hours) once an incident is flagged.
   - Internal escalation and impact assessment: 24–72 hours.
   - Customer notification (if customer data affected): typical window is within 72 hours of confirmed impact; for incidents meeting legal/regulatory thresholds we target notification within 24–48 hours of confirmation.

   I'm also attaching a short IR runbook excerpt and the BCP overview for your review (redwood-ir-runbook-v1.docx, bcp-overview.pdf). Full playbook is on our internal drive; here's a link to the shared playbook folder: https://drive.redwood.com/s/IR-playbook-xyz

3) Vendor questionnaire: happy to start. Ben will coordinate answers and Rishi (security) will own technical responses. Suggested turnaround: 5 business days for the initial pass, faster on clarifications.

4) HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads under a standard BAA; we're happy to engage legal. For GDPR/data residency, we have EU regions and can provision data residency controls — please flag which assets/processes you're most concerned about.

Next steps:
- Ben will upload the SOC2 summary and runbook excerpts to the Drive and share links.
- Rishi will take the vendor questionnaire and send back an initial pass by Tue next week.
- I'll propose a 30-minute follow-up call to run through any high-priority procurement questions — are you available Fri 11am PT?

Thanks,

Thanks for the note. Quick answers and attachments included.

- Example breach notice: attached a short draft you can share with legal (example-breach-notice-draft.txt). We generally follow a facts-first template: what happened, scope of data, remediation steps, and POC for follow-up. We can accept reasonable contract language to tighten notification windows if needed for regulated workflows.

- SOC 2: Many customers accept the SOC2 summary + attestation timeline to move through procurement; if Pioneer requires the full Type II report before signature we'll coordinate with our compliance team and provide it under NDA once available.
